verdict.summary:
SINGLE-COUNTERPARTY CREDIT LIMIT WORKPAPER — 12 CFR PART 252, SUBPART H
Draft for review by a qualified finance/regulatory-reporting professional. Not financial, tax or investment advice.

====================================================================
0. SCOPE, PERIOD, CURRENCY, BASIS
====================================================================
- Rule set: 12 CFR Part 252, Subpart H (Single-Counterparty Credit Limits), §§ 252.70–252.76, as in force 2026-11-21 (Ask 1 constraint).
- Entity: a "covered company" per § 252.70(a)(2)(i) — i.e., a global systemically important BHC, a Category II BHC, or a Category III BHC. (Classification is an assumption; see A-3.)
- Period: a single as-of date — the quarter-end reporting date as of which tier 1 capital is measured. The request supplies no date; all figures are treated as of one and the same date (A-4).
- Currency: USD, all inputs and outputs, no FX translation (A-6).
- Basis: regulatory tier 1 capital of the covered company (denominator of the test) and regulatory aggregate net credit exposure (ANCE) to one counterparty (numerator). Both on the regulatory measurement basis of Subpart H, not GAAP balance-sheet amounts.

====================================================================
1. AUTHORITY APPLIED, AND VERSION CONTROL FOR "AS IN FORCE ON 2026-11-21"
====================================================================
1.1 § 252.72(a) — Credit exposure limits, general limit (quoted verbatim):
    "No covered company may have an aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 25 percent of the tier 1 capital of the covered company."
    Source: eCFR § 252.72 (fetched 2026-11-23T04:23:39Z, sha256 cfa98394af04); identical text in CFR 2025 print, 12 CFR Ch. II (1-1-25 Edition), at § 252.72 (sha256 5ae645463357).

1.2 § 252.72(b) — conditional higher-tier limit (quoted verbatim), carried here only so it is not overlooked:
    "No major covered company may have aggregate net credit exposure to any major counterparty that exceeds 15 percent of the tier 1 capital of the major covered company."
    § 252.70(a)(2)(ii): "Major covered company means any covered company that is a global systemically important BHC."
    Relevance: conditional on (i) the covered company being a GSIB BHC and (ii) the counterparty being a "major counterparty". Neither fact is given. See § 7 caveat C-1 and the sensitivity in § 5.

1.3 § 252.76(a)(1) — the 5% assessment trigger (quoted verbatim):
    "If a covered company has an aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 5 percent of its tier 1 capital, the covered company must assess its relationship with the counterparty under paragraph (b)(2) of this section to determine whether the counterparty is economically interdependent with one or more other counterparties of the covered company and under paragraph (c)(1) of this section to determine whether the counterparty is connected by a control relationship with one or more other counterparties."
    Source: eCFR § 252.76 (fetched 2026-11-23T04:23:39Z, sha256 ca40090fa22e); identical in CFR 2025 print.

1.4 § 252.76(a)(2) — consequence of a positive assessment (quoted verbatim, abridged):
    "...the covered company must aggregate its net credit exposure to the counterparties for all purposes under this subpart, including, but not limited to, § 252.72."

1.5 Definition of economic interdependence (§ 252.76(b), quoted verbatim):
    "...two counterparties are economically interdependent if the failure, default, insolvency, or material financial distress of one counterparty would cause the failure, default, insolvency, or material financial distress of the other counterparty, taking into account the factors in paragraph (b)(2) of this section."

1.6 § 252.76(b)(2) factors retrieved verbatim (partial — see caveat C-3):
    (ii) whether counterparty A has fully or partly guaranteed the credit exposure of counterparty B, or is liable by other means, in an amount that is 50 percent or more of the covered company's net credit exposure to counterparty A;
    (iii) whether 25 percent or more of one counterparty's production or output is sold to the other counterparty, which cannot easily be replaced by other customers;
    (iv) whether the expected source of funds to repay the loans of both counterparties is the same and neither counterparty has another independent source of income from which the loans may be serviced and fully repaid;
    (v) whether two or more counterparties rely on the same source for the majority of their funding and, in the event of the common provider's default, an alternative provider cannot be found.

1.7 § 252.76(c)/(d) control-relationship indicia retrieved verbatim (§ 252.76(d)(2)): counterparty A (i) "Controls the power to vote 25 percent or more of any class of voting securities of Counterparty B pursuant to a voting agreement"; (ii) "Has significant influence on the appointment or dismissal of counterparty B's administrative, management, or governing body, or the fact that a majority of members of such body have been appointed solely as a result of the exercise of counterparty A's voting rights"; or (iii) "Has the power to exercise a controlling influence over the management or policies of counterparty B." The Board may also make its own aggregation determination under § 252.76(d)(1)–(2) after notice and opportunity for hearing.

1.8 Version-control statement. Both retrievals — the eCFR point-in-time-agnostic "current" text pulled 2026-11-23 (two days after the as-of date) and the CFR 2025 print (1-1-25 edition) — contain byte-identical operative language for §§ 252.72(a), 252.72(b) and 252.76(a)(1). Two consequences: (a) no amendment to these provisions took effect between 1 January 2025 and the 2026-11-21 as-of date on the evidence retrieved; (b) the quoted text is the text in force on 2026-11-21. Limitation: a complete amendatory-history check of Part 252 (Federal Register slips through 2026-11-21) was not performed; see caveat C-2. Subpart H source note: "83 FR 38493, Aug. 6, 2018, unless otherwise noted."

====================================================================
2. INPUTS AND PROVENANCE
====================================================================
Line | Input | Value | Unit | Source / basis | Status
I-1  | Tier 1 capital of the covered company (T1) | 40,000,000,000 | USD | Stated in the request | GIVEN
I-2  | Aggregate net credit exposure to the single counterparty (ANCE) | 11,000,000,000 | USD | Stated in the request | GIVEN
I-3  | General limit percentage | 25% (0.25) | ratio | § 252.72(a), verbatim § 1.1 | RULE
I-4  | Assessment trigger percentage | 5% (0.05) | ratio | § 252.76(a)(1), verbatim § 1.3 | RULE
I-5  | Conditional major-counterparty limit | 15% (0.15) | ratio | § 252.72(b), verbatim § 1.2 | RULE, conditionally applicable
I-6  | As-of date | single quarter-end | date | Assumed, not stated in request | ASSUMPTION A-4

Nothing in I-1 or I-2 is re-derived here: both are taken at face value as the regulatory measures. Whether they are in fact the correct regulatory measures is the subject of assumptions A-1, A-2, A-3, A-5.

====================================================================
3. COMPUTATION A — THE 25% CAP IN DOLLARS (Ask 2)
====================================================================
Formula (from § 252.72(a)):  Cap(25%) = 0.25 x T1
Step A-1: 0.25 x 40,000,000,000 = 10,000,000,000
Step A-2: Cap(25%) = USD 10,000,000,000 (= USD 10.0 billion)
Cross-check: 10,000,000,000 / 40,000,000,000 = 0.25 exactly. OK.

ANSWER TO ASK 2: USD 10,000,000,000 (USD 10.0 billion), being 25% of USD 40.0 billion of tier 1 capital, per § 252.72(a) as in force 2026-11-21.

====================================================================
4. COMPUTATION B — THE EXCESS OVER THE CAP (Ask 3)
====================================================================
Formula: Excess = ANCE - Cap(25%)
Step B-1: 11,000,000,000 - 10,000,000,000 = 1,000,000,000
Step B-2: Excess = USD 1,000,000,000 (= USD 1.0 billion) — a breach of § 252.72(a).

Supporting ratios (all derived from I-1/I-2, all internally consistent):
Step B-3: ANCE / T1 = 11,000,000,000 / 40,000,000,000 = 0.2750 = 27.50%
Step B-4: Percentage-point breach = 27.50% - 25.00% = 2.50 pp of tier 1 capital
Step B-5: Check B-4 against B-1: 2.50% x 40,000,000,000 = 1,000,000,000 = B-1. Consistent.
Step B-6: ANCE / Cap = 11,000,000,000 / 10,000,000,000 = 110.0% of the cap; i.e., the exposure is 10.0% above the cap.

ANSWER TO ASK 3: The exposure exceeds the 25% cap by USD 1,000,000,000 (USD 1.0 billion); ANCE is 110.0% of the cap and 27.50% of tier 1 capital.

====================================================================
5. COMPUTATION C — THE 5% ECONOMIC-INTERDEPENDENCE / CONTROL-RELATIONSHIP ASSESSMENT (Ask 4)
====================================================================
5.1 The test in § 252.76(a)(1) is purely arithmetic and purely a threshold test on ANCE versus 5% of tier 1 capital. It is NOT a 5% exposure cap: Subpart H contains no 5% ceiling on exposure. The 5% figure triggers a mandatory assessment and, if the assessment is positive, mandatory aggregation under § 252.76(a)(2).

5.2 Arithmetic:
Step C-1: Trigger threshold = 0.05 x T1 = 0.05 x 40,000,000,000 = 2,000,000,000
Step C-2: Test: is ANCE > threshold? 11,000,000,000 > 2,000,000,000 -> TRUE
Step C-3: Headroom / overage = 11,000,000,000 - 2,000,000,000 = 9,000,000,000 (exposure exceeds the 5% trigger by USD 9.0 billion)
Step C-4: ANCE / T1 = 27.50% (Step B-3) versus 5.00% -> 22.50 pp above the trigger; 5.50x the trigger (11.0 / 2.0).

5.3 Verdict: TRIGGERED. The covered company is required by § 252.76(a)(1) to assess its relationship with this counterparty under § 252.76(b)(2) (economic interdependence) and § 252.76(c)(1) (control relationship). The obligation is unconditional once the threshold is crossed; there is no materiality or proportionality relief in the text retrieved.

5.4 What the verdict does NOT say — and must not be read to say. Two distinct questions:
  (i) Is the ASSESSMENT OBLIGATION triggered? -> YES, arithmetic, answered above.
  (ii) IS the counterparty in fact economically interdependent with, or control-connected to, another counterparty? -> NOT DETERMINABLE from the facts supplied. The request gives no information on guarantees, output/customer concentration, common funding sources, common repayment sources, voting agreements, board influence or controlling influence (§§ 1.6–1.7). The correct treatment is therefore: assessment required, conclusion pending the documented § 252.76(b)(2)/(c)(1) analysis.

5.5 Practical consequence if the assessment is positive. § 252.76(a)(2) requires aggregation "for all purposes under this subpart, including, but not limited to, § 252.72." Because ANCE to this single counterparty is already USD 11.0 billion against a USD 10.0 billion cap, ANY positive exposure to an aggregated affiliate/connected counterparty widens the breach dollar-for-dollar. Aggregation cannot cure the existing breach; it can only enlarge it. The aggregated exposure must also be tested against the same 25% cap (USD 10.0 billion) and against the 15% cap if § 252.72(b) applies.

====================================================================
6. ANSWERS TO THE ASKS (restated)
====================================================================
Ask 1 [constraint, satisfied]: Rules applied are 12 CFR §§ 252.70, 252.72 and 252.76 as in force 2026-11-21; text pinned to two independent retrievals with identical operative language (§ 1.8).
Ask 2 [value]: 25% cap = USD 10,000,000,000 (0.25 x USD 40,000,000,000).
Ask 3 [value]: Excess = USD 1,000,000,000 (USD 11,000,000,000 - USD 10,000,000,000).
Ask 4 [verdict]: TRIGGERED — 5% threshold = USD 2,000,000,000 (0.05 x USD 40,000,000,000); ANCE of USD 11,000,000,000 exceeds it by USD 9,000,000,000, so the § 252.76(a)(1) assessment is mandatory. Whether the counterparty is in fact economically interdependent or control-connected is not determinable on the facts supplied and is not asserted.

====================================================================
7. SENSITIVITIES (each with its arithmetic; none of these is the answer to an ask)
====================================================================
S-1 Tier 1 capital sensitivity (cap = 0.25 x T1; excess = 11.0 - cap):
  T1 = USD 40.0B -> cap 10.0 -> excess +1.0 (base case, breached)
  T1 = USD 44.0B -> cap 11.0 -> excess 0.0 (breakeven: 11.0 / 0.25 = 44.0)
  T1 = USD 48.0B -> cap 12.0 -> excess -1.0 (compliant)
  Reading: each USD 1.0B of tier 1 capital moves the cap by USD 0.25B. To reach breakeven without reducing exposure, tier 1 capital must rise by USD 4.0B.

S-2 Conditional 15% limit, § 252.72(b) (applies ONLY if the covered company is a "major covered company" = GSIB BHC AND the counterparty is a "major counterparty"):
  Cap(15%) = 0.15 x 40,000,000,000 = 6,000,000,000
  Excess = 11,000,000,000 - 6,000,000,000 = 5,000,000,000
  ANCE / T1 = 27.50% vs 15.00% -> 12.50 pp above; 1.833x the 15% cap (11.0 / 6.0).
  Note: the 25% general limit of § 252.72(a) and the 15% limit of § 252.72(b) are cumulative — compliance requires satisfying both where both apply; the 15% limit would be the binding constraint. This sensitivity is disclosed, not adopted, because the classification facts are absent (A-3).

S-3 If the USD 11.0B is a GROSS figure rather than the regulatory ANCE: the § 252.73–252.75 reductions (eligible collateral, eligible guarantees, eligible credit/equity derivatives) must be at least USD 1,000,000,000 to bring net exposure to the USD 10.0B cap. Break-even offset = 11.0 - 10.0 = 1.0. The request as drafted presents USD 11.0B as the aggregate net credit exposure (A-2).

S-4 Cure arithmetic for the 25% breach (illustrative, not advice):
  (a) Reduce ANCE by >= USD 1,000,000,000 (to <= USD 10,000,000,000); or
  (b) Raise tier 1 capital by >= USD 4,000,000,000 (to >= USD 44,000,000,000), verified at Step B/A: 0.25 x 44.0 = 11.0 = ANCE; or
  (c) A combination: e.g., +USD 2.0B tier 1 (cap 10.5) with a USD 0.5B exposure reduction (ANCE 10.5) -> 10.5 vs 10.5, exactly at the limit (the limit is "exceeds", so equality is compliant).

====================================================================
8. ASSUMPTIONS REGISTER (each number above is either GIVEN, RULE, or one of these)
====================================================================
A-1 The USD 40.0B is "tier 1 capital" as defined for Subpart H purposes (§ 252.71 definitions, by reference to the Board's regulatory capital rules). Effect if wrong: cap moves USD 0.25B per USD 1.0B of capital (S-1). The § 252.71 definition text was not among the retrieved excerpts.
A-2 The USD 11.0B is already the regulatory AGGREGATE NET CREDIT EXPOSURE under §§ 252.73–252.75 (i.e., after eligible collateral, guarantee and derivative reductions and after any SPV look-through under § 252.75). Effect if wrong: see S-3.
A-3 The entity is a "covered company" under § 252.70(a)(2)(i) and is NOT a "major covered company" facing a "major counterparty" under § 252.72(b). Effect if wrong: the 15% limit applies and the binding cap is USD 6.0B (S-2).
A-4 Tier 1 capital and ANCE are measured as of the same quarter-end as-of date, and that date falls after the Subpart H compliance commencement date. § 252.70(c)(1)(i): a company that was a covered company as of 5 October 2018 had to comply from 1 July 2020; § 252.70(c) (second paragraph): a company that becomes a covered company after 5 October 2018 must comply from the first day of the ninth calendar quarter after it becomes a covered company, unless accelerated or extended by the Board in writing. Effect if wrong: if compliance had not yet commenced on 2026-11-21, no breach exists and asks 2–4 would be moot for that date.
A-5 No transition, phase-in, grandfathering, exemption or exclusion applies to this counterparty or this exposure as of 2026-11-21 (no exempt-counterparty status under § 252.71; no Board relief in writing). Effect if wrong: the exposure may be excluded or reduced, changing B-1 and C-2.
A-6 All amounts are USD on a consistent basis, no FX translation, no off-balance-sheet items omitted from ANCE.
A-7 The counterparty is a single counterparty and is not already the product of an aggregation under § 252.76. Effect if wrong: the aggregated group's exposure is >= USD 11.0B, so both the 25% breach (B-1) and the 5% trigger overage (C-3) can only be equal or larger.

====================================================================
9. CAVEATS FOR THE REVIEWER
====================================================================
C-1 Classification gap (most material). The request does not state whether the covered company is a GSIB BHC and whether the counterparty is a "major counterparty". If both are true, § 252.72(b) sets a 15% limit (USD 6.0B) that is stricter than the 25% limit reported in Ask 2. Ask 2 answers the 25% cap as asked; the reviewer must confirm that the 25% limit, not the 15% limit, is the operative constraint before relying on the USD 1.0B excess figure.
C-2 Version control. The as-of-date text was corroborated by two retrievals with identical operative language, but a full Federal Register amendatory-history review of Part 252 through 2026-11-21 was not performed. Confirm no intervening amendment to §§ 252.72 or 252.76 before filing.
C-3 Incomplete factor list. § 252.76(b)(2)(i) was not captured in the retrieved excerpt; § 1.6 lists only (ii)–(v). The assessment workpaper must be built from the full rule text, not from this memo's partial quotation.
C-4 "Exceeds" is strict. At exactly USD 10,000,000,000 the 25% limit is satisfied and there is no excess; at exactly USD 2,000,000,000 the § 252.76(a)(1) assessment is not required. The base case is USD 1.0B and USD 9.0B above those points respectively, so the strict-inequality reading does not change any answer here.
C-5 This memo sizes the breach; it does not opine on consequences, remediation obligations, or any notification requirement, which are outside the four asks.

====================================================================
10. REVIEW CHECKLIST (tie-out points)
====================================================================
[ ] Confirm the USD 40.0B is regulatory tier 1 capital per § 252.71 and its as-of date.
[ ] Confirm the USD 11.0B is the post-netting/eligible-collateral ANCE per §§ 252.73–252.75.
[ ] Confirm covered-company category and counterparty category (25% vs 15% binding limit).
[ ] Confirm compliance commencement date under § 252.70(c).
[ ] Document the § 252.76(b)(2)/(c)(1) assessment — required because ANCE (USD 11.0B) exceeds USD 2.0B — and record the conclusion (interdependent / not interdependent / Board determination), including any § 252.76(c)(2)–(3) written request for a Board determination of non-interdependence.
[ ] Re-perform: 0.25 x 40.0 = 10.0; 11.0 - 10.0 = 1.0; 0.05 x 40.0 = 2.0; 11.0 - 2.0 = 9.0; 11.0 / 40.0 = 27.5%.

quotes.text: Perquisites and personal benefits may be excluded as long as the total value of all perquisites and personal benefits for a named executive officer is less than $10,000. If the total value of all perquisites and personal benefits is $10,000 or more for any named executive officer, then each perquisite or personal benefit, regardless of its amount, must be identified by type. quotes.whole: Perquisites and personal benefits may be excluded as long as the total value of all perquisites and personal benefits for a named executive officer is less than $10,000. If the total value of all perquisites and personal benefits is $10,000 or more for any named executive officer, then each perquisite or personal benefit, regardless of its amount, must be identified by type. If perquisites and personal benefits are required to be reported for a named executive officer pursuant to this rule, then each perquisite or personal benefit that exceeds the greater of $25,000 or 10% of the total amount of perquisites and personal benefits for that officer must be quantified and disclosed in a footnote. The requirements for identification and quantification apply only to compensation for the last fiscal year. Perquisites and other personal benefits shall be valued on the basis of the aggregate incremental cost to the registrant. With respect to the perquisite or other personal benefit for which footnote quantification is required, the registrant shall describe in the footnote its methodology for computing the aggregate incremental cost. Reimbursements of taxes owed with respect to perquisites or other personal benefits must be included in column (i) and are subject to separate quantification and identification as tax reimbursements (paragraph (c)(2)(ix)(B) of this Item) even if the associated perquisites or other personal benefits are not required to be included because the total amount of all perquisites or personal benefits for an individual named executive officer is less than $10,000 or are required to be identified but are not required to be separately quantified.

quotes.whole: Perquisites and personal benefits may be excluded as long as the total value of all perquisites and personal benefits for a named executive officer is less than $10,000. quotes.whole:
Instructions to Item 402(k)(2)(vii). 1. Programs in which registrants agree to make donations to one or more charitable institutions in a director's name, payable by the registrant currently or upon a designated event, such as the retirement or death of the director, are charitable awards programs or director legacy programs for purposes of the disclosure required by paragraph (k)(2)(vii)(G) of this Item. Provide footnote disclosure of the total dollar amount payable under the program and other material terms of each such program for which tabular disclosure is provided.
2. Any item reported for a director pursuant to paragraph (k)(2)(vii) of this Item that is not a perquisite or personal benefit and whose value exceeds $10,000 must be identified and quantified in a footnote to column (g). All items of compensation are required to be included in the Director Compensation Table without regard to whether such items are required to be identified other than as specifically noted in this Item.

verdict.summary:
MEMORANDUM — ITEM 402(c) PERQUISITE ANALYSIS: EXCLUSION, QUANTIFICATION THRESHOLD, AND ITEM-BY-ITEM TEST

Prepared by: Accountant (draft for a qualified finance/accounting or securities professional to review). This is not legal, tax or investment advice.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. SCOPE, PERIOD, CURRENCY, BASIS, AUTHORITY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Registrant: an unnamed reporting company subject to Regulation S-K Item 402(c) executive compensation disclosure (full-form Summary Compensation Table). If the registrant is a smaller reporting company using the scaled table, see the note in §7 — the thresholds are the same.
- Period: a single fiscal year — the last completed fiscal year covered by the relevant proxy/information statement (assumed; the rule itself limits identification and quantification to 'compensation for the last fiscal year').
- Currency: US dollars (USD), assumed. All three given figures ($120,000; $24,000; $26,000) are treated as USD for the same fiscal year.
- Basis of measurement: aggregate incremental cost to the registrant, which is the mandated valuation basis for perquisites and personal benefits.
- Authority: 17 CFR 229.402 (Item 402). Text relied on was retrieved from eCFR 'current' on 2026-11-23T04:27:33Z (sha256 975472248ee6) and cross-checked against the 2024 and 2021 annual CFR editions on govinfo (sha256 18657eacefe1; bf0c17cb7b0e). All three carry identical language for the $10,000 exclusion gate and the $25,000 / 10% quantification test. Because the retrieved 'current' text — which reflects amendments effective on or before 2026-11-23 — contains no amendment to those thresholds, the text in force on 2026-11-21 is taken to be as quoted below. Verify against the Federal Register/CFR at the filing date before issuance.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. FACTS AS GIVEN
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
| Ref | Item | Amount (USD) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Total perquisites and personal benefits, one NEO, one fiscal year | 120,000 | Given |
| F2 | Item A | 24,000 | Given; assumed to be a perquisite/personal benefit |
| F3 | Item B | 26,000 | Given; assumed to be a perquisite/personal benefit |
| F4 | Residual other perquisites (derived) | 70,000 | 120,000 − 24,000 − 26,000 = 70,000 |
Tie-out: 24,000 + 26,000 + 70,000 = 120,000 ✓ (agrees to F1).
Assumed (flag for confirmation): neither F2 nor F3 is a tax reimbursement, an above-market-earnings item, a defined-benefit plan benefit, or an item reportable in another Summary Compensation Table column; and neither is an ordinary-course business item excluded from the perquisite definition. Either change alters the footnote treatment — see §6.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. THE RULE, QUOTED (17 CFR 229.402)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2.1 Inclusion/exclusion gate — aggregate < $10,000
- 'Perquisites and other personal benefits, or property, unless the aggregate amount of such compensation is less than $10,000' — enumeration within paragraph (c)(2)(ix).
- 'Perquisites and other personal benefits or property may be excluded only if the aggregate amount of such compensation will be less than $10,000. Individual perquisites and personal benefits shall be identified and quantified as required by Instruction 4 to paragraph (c)(2)(ix) of this Item.'

2.2 Instruction 4 to paragraph (c)(2)(ix) — the three-tier structure
'Perquisites and personal benefits may be excluded as long as the total value of all perquisites and personal benefits for a named executive officer is less than $10,000. If the total value of all perquisites and personal benefits is $10,000 or more for any named executive officer, then each perquisite or personal benefit, regardless of its amount, must be identified by type. If perquisites and personal benefits are required to be reported for a named executive officer pursuant to this rule, then each perquisite or personal benefit that exceeds the greater of $25,000 or 10% of the total amount of perquisites and personal benefits for that officer must be quantified and disclosed in a footnote. The requirements for identification and quantification apply only to compensation for the last fiscal year. Perquisites and other personal benefits shall be valued on the basis of the aggregate incremental cost to the registrant. With respect to the perquisite or other personal benefit for which footnote quantification is required, the registrant shall describe in the footnote its methodology for computing the aggregate incremental cost.'

2.3 Non-perquisite items reported in column (i)
'Any item reported for a named executive officer pursuant to paragraph (c)(2)(ix) of this Item that is not a perquisite or personal benefit and whose value exceeds $10,000 must be identified and quantified in a footnote to column (i).'

2.4 Tax reimbursements
Reimbursements of taxes owed with respect to perquisites or other personal benefits must be included in column (i) and are subject to separate quantification and identification as tax reimbursements even if the associated perquisites are excluded (aggregate < $10,000) or are identified but not separately quantified.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. APPLICATION — STEP BY STEP WITH ARITHMETIC
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Step 1 — Can the $120,000 be excluded altogether?
Test: F1 < $10,000?
120,000 < 10,000 → FALSE (120,000 ≥ 10,000).
Result: The exclusion is NOT available. The entire $120,000 is reported in column (i) 'All Other Compensation' of the Summary Compensation Table; no perquisite or personal benefit may be omitted from that column total.

Step 2 — Identification by type (applies because Step 1 failed)
Because the aggregate is ≥ $10,000, EACH perquisite or personal benefit, 'regardless of its amount', must be identified by type in a footnote to column (i) — including Item A ($24,000), Item B ($26,000), and every constituent of the $70,000 residual. Identification by type is required even where individual quantification is not.

Step 3 — Compute the footnote quantification threshold
10% prong: 0.10 × 120,000 = 12,000.
Greater-of test: max(25,000; 12,000) = 25,000.
Applicable threshold for this NEO = $25,000.
(Cross-check on which prong binds: the 10% prong exceeds $25,000 only when total perquisites exceed 25,000 ÷ 0.10 = 250,000. At exactly 250,000 the two prongs are equal (0.10 × 250,000 = 25,000). Since 120,000 < 250,000, the flat $25,000 prong governs here.)

Step 4 — Item-by-item quantification test (each item tested separately, not in aggregate)
| Item | Amount (USD) | Comparison with threshold | Exceeds? | Required treatment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Item A | 24,000 | 24,000 − 25,000 = (1,000) | No | Identify by type in footnote to column (i); no individual quantification |
| Item B | 26,000 | 26,000 − 25,000 = 1,000 | Yes | Quantify in footnote to column (i) AND describe the methodology for computing aggregate incremental cost |
| Residual perquisites | 70,000 total | Each constituent tested individually against 25,000 | Data-dependent | Identify each by type; quantify any single constituent exceeding 25,000 |
Note on the residual: the $70,000 is an aggregate of items not separately specified. The rule tests each perquisite individually, so a constituent of, e.g., $30,000 would require quantification even though the $24,000 item does not. Confirm the composition of the $70,000 before concluding that Item B is the only quantified item.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. ANSWERS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4.1 May the registrant exclude perquisites altogether? — NO. Perquisites and personal benefits may be excluded only if the aggregate for the NEO is less than $10,000. Here the aggregate is $120,000 (120,000 ≥ 10,000), so the full $120,000 is included in column (i) and every perquisite is identified by type. The rule permits exclusion only below $10,000 in aggregate; it never permits omitting perquisites from the column when the aggregate reaches $10,000.

4.2 Footnote quantification threshold — $25,000. Derived as the greater of $25,000 or 10% of the NEO's total perquisites and personal benefits: max(25,000; 0.10 × 120,000 = 12,000) = $25,000.

4.3 Which item must be quantified — the $26,000 item. $26,000 > $25,000 (exceeds by $1,000), so it must be quantified in a footnote with a description of the aggregate incremental cost methodology. The $24,000 item does not exceed $25,000 (short by $1,000) and is identified by type only, not quantified.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. ILLUSTRATIVE FOOTNOTE (MODEL LANGUAGE — TO BE COMPLETED WITH ACTUAL TYPES AND COSTS)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
'Footnote to column (i) — Perquisites and Personal Benefits.
The amount reported in column (i) includes perquisites and other personal benefits with an aggregate incremental cost to the registrant of $120,000 for the fiscal year ended [date], valued on the basis of aggregate incremental cost. These consist of the following types: [type 1], [type 2], [type 3] and [type 4]. Because the aggregate value of perquisites and personal benefits equals or exceeds $10,000, each perquisite and personal benefit is identified by type regardless of amount. The [describe $26,000 item] had an aggregate incremental cost of $26,000, which exceeds the greater of $25,000 or 10% of total perquisites and personal benefits ($12,000), and is quantified as follows: $26,000, computed as [methodology — e.g., incremental charter hours × hourly rate + incremental catering = $X + $Y = $26,000]. The remaining perquisites and personal benefits are identified by type but not separately quantified because none individually exceeds $25,000, the greater of $25,000 and 10% of total perquisites and personal benefits ($12,000).'

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. SENSITIVITIES / WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- If total perquisites were below $10,000: exclusion from column (i) would be available, but tax reimbursements on excluded perquisites would still require separate quantification.
- If total perquisites exceeded $250,000: the 10% prong would exceed $25,000 and would govern (threshold = 0.10 × total).
- If Item A ($24,000) were a tax reimbursement rather than a perquisite: it would require separate identification and quantification as a tax reimbursement irrespective of the $25,000 test.
- If Item A ($24,000) were a non-perquisite item reported in column (i): the separate $10,000 test for non-perquisite column (i) items would require its identification and quantification (24,000 > 10,000).
- If either item were an ordinary-course business item or otherwise outside the perquisite definition: it would drop out of the $120,000 base, changing the 10% prong (though not the $25,000 floor at these magnitudes).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. SMALLER REPORTING COMPANY NOTE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The scaled smaller-reporting-company paragraph of Item 402 (paragraph (n), per the cross-references in the retrieved text) contains the same operative thresholds — exclusion only if the aggregate is less than $10,000, identification by type at $10,000 or more, and quantification of each item exceeding the greater of $25,000 or 10% of the officer's total perquisites. The conclusions in §4 therefore do not change; only the table (scaled Summary Compensation Table) and column reference change.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Confirm the nature of the $24,000 and $26,000 items (perquisite vs. personal benefit vs. tax reimbursement vs. other column (i) item).
2. Confirm the composition of the $70,000 residual and test each constituent against $25,000.
3. Confirm fiscal year, currency and that all amounts are aggregate incremental cost.
4. Confirm filer status (full-form vs. smaller reporting company) and confirm no intervening amendment to Item 402 between the retrieved text and 2026-11-21.

quotes.whole:
(d) Advanced approaches capital ratio calculations.  An advanced approaches national bank or Federal savings association that has completed the parallel run process and received notification from the OCC pursuant to § 3.121(d) must determine its regulatory capital ratios as described in paragraphs (d)(1) through (3) of this section.
(1) Common equity tier 1 capital ratio.  The national bank's or Federal savings association's common equity tier 1 capital ratio is the lower of:
(i) The ratio of the national bank's or Federal savings association's common equity tier 1 capital to standardized total risk-weighted assets; and
(ii) The ratio of the national bank's or Federal savings association's common equity tier 1 capital to advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets.
(2) Tier 1 capital ratio.  The national bank's or Federal savings association's tier 1 capital ratio is the lower of:
(i) The ratio of the national bank's or Federal savings association's tier 1 capital to standardized total risk-weighted assets; and
(ii) The ratio of the national bank's or Federal savings association's tier 1 capital to advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets.

verdict.summary:
MEMO — 2014 MINIMUM CET1 AND TIER 1 RATIOS, ADVANCED APPROACHES NATIONAL BANK (NOT A SLHC), OCC 12 CFR PART 3
Draft for review by a qualified regulatory-capital professional. Not legal, tax or investment advice.

=====================================================================
1. SCOPE, PERIOD, CURRENCY, BASIS
=====================================================================
Entity: a national bank that is an 'advanced approaches national bank' and is NOT a savings and loan holding company. Regulator/rule text: OCC, 12 CFR Part 3 (the OCC's Basel III rule, source 78 FR 62157, Oct. 11, 2013).
Period: January 1, 2014 through December 31, 2014 inclusive.
Currency: not applicable. All figures are dimensionless regulatory ratios expressed as a percentage of risk-weighted assets (or, for the leverage ratio, of average total consolidated assets). No currency amount is stated anywhere in this memo.
Basis: minimum regulatory capital ratio under Part 3, measured on the denominator the rule prescribes for that ratio (advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets per § 3.1(f)(1)(i) and § 3.10(d), and standardized total risk-weighted assets per § 3.10(b) once applicable). Ratios are not annualized, not time-weighted, and not averaged — they are the floor that must be maintained at all times during the period.
Excluded by instruction (ask 3): the capital conservation buffer, any countercyclical capital buffer amount, any G-SIB surcharge, and any other add-on. See section 6 for the textual support that these did not attach in 2014.

=====================================================================
2. ANSWERS (bottom line)
=====================================================================
ASK 1 — Minimum ratios that APPLIED during 1 Jan 2014 – 31 Dec 2014 (transition/phase-in minimums):
    Common equity tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio .... 4.0 percent
    Tier 1 capital ratio ......................... 5.5 percent
    (context, not requested: total capital ratio 8 percent; leverage ratio 4 percent)

ASK 2 — Corresponding minimum ratios stated in the text of 12 CFR Part 3 as reproduced on the cited page (the steady-state / fully phased-in general minimums in § 3.10(a)(1)):
    Common equity tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio .... 4.5 percent
    Tier 1 capital ratio ......................... 6.0 percent
    (context, not requested: total capital ratio 8 percent; leverage ratio 4 percent; supplementary leverage ratio 3 percent for advanced approaches banks)

The two pairs are NOT the same, and that is the substantive point of the exercise: the page's headline minimums (4.5 / 6.0) are the steady-state floors, while the floors actually binding on this bank during calendar 2014 were the transitional floors (4.0 / 5.5). A legacy checklist that carries 4.5 / 6.0 into a 2014 column overstates the 2014 requirement; one that carries 4.0 / 5.5 into a post-2014 column understates it.

=====================================================================
3. SOURCE TEXT FOR EACH FIGURE (verbatim)
=====================================================================
[A] 4.0% and 5.5% — 12 CFR § 3.1(f)(1)(iii)(A). Fetched from https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/section-3.1 (fetch 2026-11-23T04:31:26Z, sha256 4f71f982fe1a). Same sentence reproduced at https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/part-3 (sha256 9bf3368111e1), at http://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/part-3, at https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2024-title12-vol1/xhtml/CFR-2024-title12-vol1-part3.html (sha256 f74bb08d7f12), and at https://www.occ.treas.gov/news-issuances/federal-register/2014/78fr62018.pdf (sha256 e742b3bbc3c1):
    '(f) Timing. (1) Subject to the transition provisions in subpart G of this part, an advanced approaches national bank or Federal savings association that is not a savings and loan holding company must: ... (iii) Beginning on January 1, 2014, calculate and maintain minimum capital ratios in accordance with subparts A, B, and C of this part, provided, however, that such national bank or Federal savings association must: (A) From January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2014, maintain a minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4 percent, a minimum tier 1 capital ratio of 5.5 percent, a minimum total capital ratio of 8 percent, and a minimum leverage ratio of 4 percent; and (B) From January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2017, ...'
    Why this paragraph is the right one: it is scoped by its own words to 'an advanced approaches national bank ... that is not a savings and loan holding company' — exactly the entity in the request — and it fixes the dates 'January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2014'.

[B] 4.5% and 6.0% — 12 CFR § 3.10(a)(1)(i)-(ii). Fetched from https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/part-3 (sha256 9bf3368111e1) and https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2024-title12-vol1/xhtml/CFR-2024-title12-vol1-part3.html (sha256 f74bb08d7f12):
    '§ 3.10 Minimum capital requirements. (a) Minimum capital requirements. (1) A national bank or Federal savings association must maintain the following minimum capital ratios: (i) A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent. (ii) A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent. (iii) A total capital ratio of 8 percent. (iv) A leverage ratio of 4 percent. (v) For advanced approaches national banks or Federal savings associations or, for Category III OCC-regulated institutions, a supplementary leverage ratio of 3 percent.'
    And in the OCC Federal Register reproduction (78 FR 62018 PDF, sha256 e742b3bbc3c1), where the section prints as '§ l.10' with a '[BANK]' placeholder:
    'A [BANK] must maintain the following minimum capital ratios: (1) A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent. (2) A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent. (3) A total capital ratio of 8 percent. (4) A leverage ratio of 4 percent. (5) For advanced approaches [BANK]s, a supplementary leverage ratio of 3 percent.'

[C] Caveat on 'the cited page' (disclosed, not blocking). The specific page image referenced by the legacy checklist was not supplied to me. I therefore tested every candidate page in the fetched set — current eCFR § 3.1, current eCFR Part 3, govinfo CFR-2024 Part 3, and the OCC's 78 FR 62018 PDF — and all of them reproduce § 3.10(a)(1) with the identical pair 4.5 percent / 6 percent. Because the answer to ask 2 is invariant across every candidate page, the comparison is honestly answerable. If the checklist's page is a different document that states different numbers, the answer to ask 2 changes with that document and this memo must be re-run against it; ask 1 is unaffected because it rests on the transition paragraph, which is quoted identically in all five fetched sources.

=====================================================================
4. ARITHMETIC AND RECONCILIATION (every figure, every step)
=====================================================================
4.1 Presentation basis. All values below are in percentage points (pp) of the relevant risk-weighted asset denominator. Percentages are quoted directly from the rule text; none is computed, interpolated or derived.

4.2 Ask 1 vs Ask 2, ratio by ratio:
    CET1: 4.5% (ask 2, § 3.10(a)(1)(i)) − 4.0% (ask 1, § 3.1(f)(1)(iii)(A)) = 0.50 pp
    Tier 1: 6.0% (ask 2, § 3.10(a)(1)(ii)) − 5.5% (ask 1, § 3.1(f)(1)(iii)(A)) = 0.50 pp
    Both spreads are exactly 0.50 pp. No economic meaning should be read into that symmetry beyond the fact that the 2014 step sits 50 bp below the steady-state floor on both measures.

4.3 Transition as a fraction of the steady-state floor (descriptive only — NOT a regulatory formula):
    CET1: 4.0 / 4.5 = 0.8889 (88.89%)
    Tier 1: 5.5 / 6.0 = 0.9167 (91.67%)
    Both fractions are < 1.00, which is the required direction for a phase-in (the transitional floor may be equal to or lower than the steady-state floor; it may never exceed it). Neither fraction is used by the rule to set any number.

4.4 Hierarchy / consistency checks (guarding against a value that violates a bound the same memo states):
    (a) Capital-stack ordering, 2014 regime: CET1 4.0 ≤ Tier 1 5.5 ≤ Total capital 8.0 — holds (4.0 ≤ 5.5 ≤ 8.0).
    (b) Capital-stack ordering, steady state: CET1 4.5 ≤ Tier 1 6.0 ≤ Total capital 8.0 — holds (4.5 ≤ 6.0 ≤ 8.0).
    (c) Phase-in monotonicity: 4.0 ≤ 4.5 and 5.5 ≤ 6.0 — holds; neither transitional figure exceeds the figure it transitions toward.
    (d) No reported figure is a maximum, so no reported figure can exceed a ceiling stated elsewhere in this memo.

4.5 REJECTED DERIVATION — stated here so it is not substituted downstream. Subpart G's transition table contains an entry reading 'Calendar year 2014 — 80' (also 'Calendar year 2015 — 70') in the fetched text. Applying that 80 as a multiplier to the steady-state minimums would produce 4.5 × 0.80 = 3.60% and 6.0 × 0.80 = 4.80%. Those are NOT the 2014 minimums and must not be reported. The 2014 minimum ratios are hard-coded in § 3.1(f)(1)(iii)(A) as 4 percent and 5.5 percent. The subpart G percentage operates on transitional capital adjustments (e.g., the treatment of items subject to transition), not as a scalar on the headline ratio floors.

4.6 Applicability checks performed:
    (a) Advanced approaches status: § 3.1(f)(1) applies to 'an advanced approaches national bank ... that is not a savings and loan holding company' — matches the entity exactly. A non-advanced-approaches bank is not even subject to Part 3 until January 1, 2015 ('No national bank or Federal savings association that is not an advanced approaches bank or advanced approaches savings association is subject to this part 3 until January 1, 2015'), which is precisely why the 2014 floors exist only in the advanced approaches timing paragraph.
    (b) Not a SLHC: the SLHC carve-out language in § 3.1(f)(2) (supplementary leverage ratio relief for 'a savings and loan holding company that is an advanced approaches [BANK]') is inapplicable here; the correct paragraph remains (f)(1).
    (c) OCC vs Board vs FDIC text: a national bank is OCC-supervised, so 12 CFR Part 3 is the governing text (the parallel Board rule is 12 CFR part 217 and the FDIC's is 12 CFR part 324; those would apply to a state member bank or state nonmember bank, not to this entity).

=====================================================================
5. WHAT THE LEGACY CHECKLIST SHOULD CARRY (practical mapping)
=====================================================================
Column 'OCC transition standards, calendar year 2014' → CET1 4.0%, Tier 1 5.5% (citation: 12 CFR 3.1(f)(1)(iii)(A)).
Column 'minimum ratios per 12 CFR Part 3 text on the cited page' → CET1 4.5%, Tier 1 6.0% (citation: 12 CFR 3.10(a)(1)(i)-(ii)).
If the checklist has a single 'minimum' column that must hold for 2014, the correct entry is 4.0 / 5.5 — the steady-state pair did not bind until the following year. If the checklist is testing whether the reviewer can distinguish the two, both pairs must appear with their citations.

=====================================================================
6. ASK 3 — BUFFERS AND ADD-ONS EXCLUDED (textual support)
=====================================================================
(a) Capital conservation buffer: § 3.1(f) states 'Beginning on January 1, 2016, and subject to the transition provisions in subpart G of this part, a national bank or Federal savings association is subject to limitations on distributions and discretionary bonus payments with respect to its capital conservation buffer and any applicable countercyclical capital buffer amount.' No buffer constraint existed during 2014, so there is nothing to add to 4.0 / 5.5 and nothing to add to 4.5 / 6.0 for this period.
(b) Countercyclical capital buffer amount: not applicable in 2014 (same provision; no amount was in effect).
(c) Supplementary leverage ratio (3 percent for advanced approaches banks, § 3.10(a)(1)(v)): excluded — it is a leverage measure, not a CET1 or tier 1 risk-based ratio, and the transition text states that from January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2017 an advanced approaches bank 'Is not required to maintain a supplementary leverage ratio' (§ 3.1(f)(1)(iii)(B)).
(d) G-SIB surcharge and stress capital buffer: not in the 2014 rule text and not applicable to this period.
Net effect of ask 3: zero adjustment. The reported pairs are the bare minimums.

=====================================================================
7. STATUS OF THE NUMBERS — ASSUMPTIONS VS QUOTES
=====================================================================
All four reported figures (4.0, 5.5, 4.5, 6.0 percent) are direct verbatim quotations from fetched official text, not estimates, not interpolations and not assumptions. The only judgement in this memo is the identification of which page constitutes 'the cited page' for ask 2; that judgement is disclosed in section 3[C] and, because every candidate page carries the same pair, it does not change the reported value.

=====================================================================
8. ITEMS FOR PROFESSIONAL REVIEW
=====================================================================
- Confirm that the legacy checklist's cited page is one of the Part 3 reproductions tested in section 3[C]; if it is a different document, re-run ask 2 against that document.
- Confirm the entity's advanced approaches status and parallel-run status as of 1 January 2014; the minimum floors in § 3.1(f)(1)(iii)(A) apply regardless of parallel-run completion, but the ratio calculation methodology in § 3.10(d) (lower of standardized and advanced approaches ratios) applies only after parallel run and OCC notification under § 3.121(d). This affects how a ratio is computed, not the floor it must clear.
- Confirm no state or foreign supervisory minimum applied to the entity that was higher than the federal floors during 2014; such a requirement would be an add-on outside the scope of ask 3.
- This memo addresses the 2014 transition year only; it expresses no view on the 2015-2017 phase-in percentages or on any subsequent amendment to Part 3.

From 1 April 2023, there is no longer a single Corporation Tax rate for non-ring fence profits.
At the Spring Budget 2021, the Corporation Tax main rate for non-ring fence profits was increased to 25% for profits above £250,000.
A small profits rate of 19% was also announced for companies with profits of £50,000 or less.
Companies with profits between £50,000 and £250,000 will pay tax at the main rate, reduced by a marginal relief. This provides a gradual increase in the effective Corporation Tax rate.

Ring fence companies
There are different Corporation Tax rates for companies that make profits from oil extraction or oil rights in the UK or UK continental shelf. These are known as ‘ring fence’ companies.
For periods up to 31 March 2023, Marginal Relief is available to ring fence companies on profits between £300,000 and £1.5 million. From 1 April 2023, Marginal Relief is available for companies with profits between £50,000 and £250,000.

quotes.whole:
Contents
Rates
Expenses
Allowances and reliefs
Rates
The Corporation Tax rate for company profits is 25%
You pay Corporation Tax at the rates that applied in your company’s accounting period for Corporation Tax.
If your company made more than £250,000 profit, you’ll pay the main rate of Corporation Tax.
If your company made a profit of £50,000 or less, you’ll pay the ‘small profits rate’, which is 19%.
You may be entitled to ‘Marginal Relief’ if your profits were between £50,000 and £250,000.
The £50,000 and £250,000 profit thresholds are proportionately reduced for short accounting periods and by the total number of ‘associated companies’ your company has.
There are different rates for ‘ring fence’ profits of companies involved in oil rights or extraction in the UK or UK continental shelf.
You may be able to get deductions or claim tax credits on your Corporation Tax. These are known as allowances and reliefs.
Previous rates
From 1 April 2015 to 31 March 2023, a single rate of Corporation Tax applied to all companies.
The rate you pay on profits from before 1 April 2015 depends on the size of your profits.
Work out your profits when you prepare your Company Tax Return.

Contents
What Marginal Relief is
Who can claim Marginal Relief
Who cannot claim Marginal Relief
Check how much relief you can claim
What Marginal Relief is
From 1 April 2023 the Corporation Tax rate changes to:
19% for taxable profits below £50,000 (small profit rate)
25% for taxable profits above £250,000 (main rate)
Marginal Relief provides a gradual increase in Corporation Tax rate between the small profits rate and the main rate — this allows you to reduce your rate from the 25% main rate.
Who can claim Marginal Relief
Your company or organisation may be able to claim Marginal Relief if its taxable profits from 1 April 2023 are between:
£50,000 (the lower limit)
£250,000 (the upper limit)

quotes.text:
Who cannot claim Marginal Relief
You cannot claim Marginal Relief if:
you’re a non-UK resident company
you’re a close investment holding company
your profits (including distributions from unrelated, unassociated companies) go over £250,000
Check how much relief you can claim
You can calculate Marginal Relief for Corporation Tax to check how much Marginal Relief you may be able to claim.
You should only use this service to calculate Marginal Relief on Corporation Tax profits from 1 April 2023.

quotes.whole:
augmented profits - defined at CTA10/S18L as the total taxable profits plus exempt distributions of a qualifying kind received by the company that are not excluded.
Further details of what is meant by profits in this context are at CTM03915.
Where the profits do not exceed a set lower limit, the total taxable profits are charged at a lower rate of CT, known as the standard small profits rate.  This is distinguished from the small ring fence profits rate, CTA10/S279A.
Where the profits exceed a set upper limit, the total taxable profits are charged at the CT main rate.
Marginal Relief
Where profits fall between the lower and upper limits, the total taxable profits are charged at the main rate of CT and the resulting tax is reduced by a sum of marginal relief computed by applying a ‘standard fraction’ to an amount as calculated at CTM03925. More details of the circumstances in which the standard small profits rate of tax or marginal relief applies are at CTM03915 onwards.

Company C has an accounting period of 1 July 2030 to 30 June 2031, profits of £85,000 and two associated companies for the period to 31 March 2031 and one associated company for the three months to 30 June 2031.  The CT main rate and small profits are unchanged at 25% and 19% respectively but the upper limit has been raised to £300,000.
Marginal relief fraction
The differential between the lower and upper limits has changed so the marginal relief fraction for Financial Year 2031 therefore becomes:
£50,000 x 19%  = £9,500
£300,000 x 25% = £75,000
£250,000 x fraction = £65,500
£65,500/£250,000 = 26.2% marginal rate fraction
Difference between the main rate and the marginal rate expressed as a fraction is
26.2% - 25% = 1.2% = 3/250

verdict.summary:
# Corporation Tax: non-ring fence profits, rules from 1 April 2023

Draft for review by a qualified finance/accounting professional. Not financial, tax or investment advice.

## 1. Scope, period, currency, basis

| Item | Stated position |
|---|---|
| Tax | UK Corporation Tax (CT) |
| Profit stream | Non-ring fence profits only. Ring fence (oil extraction / oil rights, UK or UK continental shelf) is out of scope and its rates (19% small ring fence / 30% main ring fence / fraction 11/400) are excluded |
| Period | Financial year 2023 = **1 April 2023 to 31 March 2024**, and subsequent financial years on the same basis |
| Currency | GBP (£) |
| Basis of the figures | Taxable total profits of a UK-resident company for a single 12-month accounting period coincident with the financial year, with **no associated companies** and no exempt distributions of a qualifying kind (so augmented profits = taxable total profits). Adjustments for associated companies and short accounting periods are set out in section 6 |
| Sources | HMRC guidance as fetched (see section 8) |

## 2. Verdict (ask 4)

**No. From 1 April 2023 there is no longer a single Corporation Tax rate for non-ring fence profits.**

HMRC's words: *"From 1 April 2023, there is no longer a single Corporation Tax rate for non-ring fence profits."* (Corporation Tax rates and allowances guidance, sha256 8121e4a75038).

Corroboration: the same page's "Previous rates" text on the CT rates guide states *"From 1 April 2015 to 31 March 2023, a single rate of Corporation Tax applied to all companies"* (sha256 f9065dbe6492) — i.e. the single rate ended on 31 March 2023.

## 3. The rates (asks 5 and 6)

Per the HMRC rates table (column "2023", sha256 8121e4a75038), reproduced for the 2023 financial year:

| Band (taxable total profits, GBP, 12-month period, no associates) | Rate | Ask |
|---|---|---|
| £50,000 or less | **Small profits rate 19%** | 5 |
| Over £250,000 | **Main rate 25%** | 6 |
| £50,000 to £250,000 | Main rate 25% charged, then **reduced by marginal relief** | 7 |

Supporting quotes:
- *"A small profits rate of 19% was also announced for companies with profits of £50,000 or less."* (sha256 8121e4a75038)
- *"If your company made a profit of £50,000 or less, you'll pay the 'small profits rate', which is 19%."* (sha256 f9065dbe6492)
- *"If your company made more than £250,000 profit, you'll pay the main rate of Corporation Tax."* — the same page states *"The Corporation Tax rate for company profits is 25%"* (sha256 f9065dbe6492)
- *"From 1 April 2023 the Corporation Tax rate changes to: 19% for taxable profits below £50,000 (small profit rate); 25% for taxable profits above £250,000 (main rate)"* (Marginal Relief guidance, sha256 cc6f1af71f34)

Table parameters for FY2023 (sha256 8121e4a75038): Marginal Relief lower limit **£50,000**; upper limit **£250,000**; **standard fraction 3/200**.

Note on "£50,000 or less" vs "below £50,000": HMRC uses both formulations. It makes no difference — see the boundary proof at 4.2.

## 4. Treatment of profits between £50,000 and £250,000 (ask 7)

### 4.1 The rule

Profits in the band are charged at the **main rate of 25%**, and the resulting tax is **reduced by marginal relief**. Marginal relief produces a **gradual increase in the effective rate** from 19% to 25%.

HMRC's words:
- *"Companies with profits between £50,000 and £250,000 will pay tax at the main rate, reduced by a marginal relief. This provides a gradual increase in the effective Corporation Tax rate."* (sha256 8121e4a75038)
- *"You may be entitled to 'Marginal Relief' if your profits were between £50,000 and £250,000."* (sha256 f9065dbe6492)
- *"Marginal Relief provides a gradual increase in Corporation Tax rate between the small profits rate and the main rate — this allows you to reduce your rate from the 25% main rate."* (sha256 cc6f1af71f34)
- CTM03905: *"Where profits fall between the lower and upper limits, the total taxable profits are charged at the main rate of CT and the resulting tax is reduced by a sum of marginal relief computed by applying a 'standard fraction' to an amount..."* (sha256 fb3fe1275f68)

### 4.2 Marginal relief computation

Statutory form (CTA 2010 Part 3A), applied with the FY2023 standard fraction **3/200 = 0.015 = 1.5%**:

> Marginal relief = (U − A) × N/A × 3/200

where U = upper limit (£250,000), A = augmented profits, N = taxable total profits. Where there are no exempt distributions of a qualifying kind, A = N and the formula simplifies to:

> **Marginal relief = (250,000 − P) × 3/200**, and **CT = 0.25 × P − (250,000 − P) × 0.015**

Equivalently, in closed form for 50,000 ≤ P ≤ 250,000: **CT = 0.265 × P − 3,750**.

Provenance note: the fetched passages state the fraction (3/200) and the direction of the relief, and CTM03958's worked example applies the fraction to (upper limit − profits) — i.e. the (U − A) × F form. The full statutory wording of CTA10 s18C was not in the fetched passages; the formula above should be confirmed against the statute by the reviewer.

**Boundary proofs (these are the consistency tests for asks 5, 6 and 7):**

- At P = £50,000: 25% × 50,000 = £12,500.00; relief = (250,000 − 50,000) × 0.015 = 200,000 × 0.015 = £3,000.00; CT = £9,500.00. Check: 19% × 50,000 = £9,500.00. **Agrees exactly with the ask-5 rate — no discontinuity at the lower limit.**
- At P = £250,000: relief = (250,000 − 250,000) × 0.015 = £0.00; CT = 25% × 250,000 = £62,500.00. **Agrees exactly with the ask-6 rate — no discontinuity at the upper limit.**
- Marginal rate in the band: d/dP of (0.25P − (250,000 − P)(0.015)) = 0.25 + 0.015 = **0.265 = 26.5%**. Checked by step: P = 100,000 → CT £22,750.00; P = 100,100 → 25,025.00 − (149,900 × 0.015 = 2,248.50) = £22,776.50; Δ = £26.50 on £100 = 26.5%. ✔
- Below the lower limit the relief formula is **not** applied. At P = £40,000: 19% × 40,000 = £7,600.00. (The relief formula would give 10,000 − 210,000 × 0.015 = £6,850, which is lower — so the small profits rate, not relief, governs below £50,000.)

### 4.3 Schedule of CT — FY2023, non-ring fence, 12-month period, no associated companies

All figures GBP. Arithmetic shown in full.

| P = taxable total profits | 25% × P (main rate) | Marginal relief (250,000 − P) × 0.015 | CT due | Effective rate (CT / P) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 40,000 (below band) | n/a — 19% applies | n/a | **7,600.00** (19% × 40,000) | 19.000% |
| 50,000 (lower limit) | 12,500.00 | 200,000 × 0.015 = 3,000.00 | **9,500.00** | 19.000% |
| 60,000 | 15,000.00 | 190,000 × 0.015 = 2,850.00 | **12,150.00** | 20.250% |
| 75,000 | 18,750.00 | 175,000 × 0.015 = 2,625.00 | **16,125.00** | 21.500% |
| 100,000 | 25,000.00 | 150,000 × 0.015 = 2,250.00 | **22,750.00** | 22.750% |
| 150,000 | 37,500.00 | 100,000 × 0.015 = 1,500.00 | **36,000.00** | 24.000% |
| 200,000 | 50,000.00 | 50,000 × 0.015 = 750.00 | **49,250.00** | 24.625% |
| 250,000 (upper limit) | 62,500.00 | 0 × 0.015 = 0.00 | **62,500.00** | 25.000% |
| 300,000 (above band) | 75,000.00 | none | **75,000.00** | 25.000% |

Cross-checks: closed form 0.265P − 3,750 gives 9,500 / 22,750 / 62,500 at P = 50,000 / 100,000 / 250,000 — ties to the table. Every effective rate lies within [19%, 25%]; CT is monotonically increasing in P across all rows (7,600 → 9,500 → 12,150 → 16,125 → 22,750 → 36,000 → 49,250 → 62,500 → 75,000). Effective rate = 26.5% − 3,750/P inside the band.

### 4.4 Who cannot claim marginal relief

Per the Marginal Relief guidance (sha256 cc6f1af71f34): not available to a **non-UK resident company**, a **close investment-holding company**, or where profits (including distributions from unrelated, unassociated companies) exceed **£250,000**. CTM03905 (sha256 fb3fe1275f68) confirms the small profits rate/marginal relief scope excludes close investment-holding companies (CTA10/S18N).

## 5. Accounting periods straddling 1 April 2023

Where more than one rate applies in an accounting period, split the period by days and compute each part separately (sha256 f9065dbe6492). HMRC's own example: an accounting period 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023 uses the financial year starting 1 April 2022 rate for **90 days** (1 Jan–31 Mar 2023) and the financial year starting 1 April 2023 rate for **275 days** (1 Apr–31 Dec 2023). 90 + 275 = 365. ✔

## 6. Threshold adjustments (limits on the figures above)

HMRC: *"The £50,000 and £250,000 profit thresholds are proportionately reduced for short accounting periods and by the total number of 'associated companies' your company has"* (sha256 f9065dbe6492).

- **Short accounting period:** apportion the £50,000 / £250,000 limits by reference to the number of days in the period over 365. Example: 6-month (182-day) period → lower limit 50,000 × 182/365 = £24,931.51; upper limit 250,000 × 182/365 = £124,657.53.
- **Associated companies:** the limits are reduced by reference to the number of associated companies. *Illustrative, and to be confirmed against CTA10 s18D by the reviewer* (the fetched gov.uk text says only "by the total number of associated companies"): on the (1 + number of associates) convention, one associate gives lower £25,000 / upper £125,000; two associates give £16,666.67 / £83,333.33; and one associate with a 182-day period gives £12,465.75 / £62,328.77.
- **Augmented profits:** the upper-limit test uses augmented profits (taxable total profits plus exempt distributions of a qualifying kind that are not excluded — CTA10/S18L, per CTM03905, sha256 fb3fe1275f68). The relief formula's A term is augmented profits; N is taxable total profits.

All of section 4's figures assume no associated companies and a 12-month period, as stated in section 1.

## 7. Version control and two traps in the source pages

1. **Stale line:** the "Show all updates" list on the rates-and-allowances publication page (sha256 d589956a9326) contains a 3 October 2022 entry reading *"The Corporation Tax main rate will remain at 19% from 1 April 2023."* That was **superseded** by the 21 December 2022 entry on the same page: *"From 1 April 2023 there is no longer a single Corporation Tax rate for non-ring fence profits. Marginal relief is also available for companies with profits between £50,000 and £250,000."* The current table (19% / 25% / £50,000 / £250,000 / 3/200) governs. Do not use the 3 October 2022 line.
2. **Illustrative future example, not FY2023:** CTM03958 (sha256 7c01dd11e1de) works an example for a period 1 July 2030 to 30 June 2031 with an upper limit of **£300,000** and fraction **3/250**. That is a hypothetical future-year illustration. For FY2023 the upper limit is £250,000 and the fraction is 3/200. Do not import 3/250 or £300,000.
3. **Which version?** The guidance page is marked "Updated 1 April 2026". The 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 columns of the table all show the same values (small profits 19%, main 25%, lower limit £50,000, upper limit £250,000, standard fraction 3/200). The FY2023 answer is therefore unaffected by using the current version of the page.

## 8. Sources

All fetched 2026-11-23.

| Ref | Page | sha256 | Supports |
|---|---|---|---|
| [1] | https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/rates-and-allowances-corporation-tax/rates-and-allowances-corporation-tax | 8121e4a75038 | Rates table (19% / 25% / £50,000 / £250,000 / 3/200); "no longer a single Corporation Tax rate"; marginal relief description; ring fence rates excluded |
| [2] | https://www.gov.uk/corporation-tax-rates | f9065dbe6492 | 25% main rate; 19% small profits rate; marginal relief band; threshold reduction for short periods and associates; 90/275-day straddle example; single rate 1 Apr 2015–31 Mar 2023 |
| [3] | https://www.gov.uk/guidance/corporation-tax-marginal-relief | cc6f1af71f34 | 19% / 25%; relief mechanism; who cannot claim |
| [4] | https://www.gov.uk/hmrc-internal-manuals/company-taxation-manual/ctm03905 | fb3fe1275f68 | Statutory basis (CTA10 Part 3A, FA2021/S6 and SCH1); main-rate-plus-relief mechanism; standard fraction; augmented profits definition (CTA10/S18L); CIC exclusion (CTA10/S18N) |
| [5] | https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/rates-and-allowances-corporation-tax | d589956a9326 | Update history; 21 Dec 2022 change; the superseded 3 Oct 2022 line |
| [6] | https://www.gov.uk/hmrc-internal-manuals/company-taxation-manual/ctm03958 | 7c01dd11e1de | Confirms the fraction is applied to (upper limit − profits); source of the FY2031 £300,000 / 3/250 illustration that must not be used for FY2023 |

## 9. Answer in one line

From 1 April 2023 there is **no** single CT rate for non-ring fence profits: **19%** on profits of £50,000 or less, **25%** on profits above £250,000, and for profits between £50,000 and £250,000 tax is charged at the **25% main rate reduced by marginal relief** at the standard fraction **3/200** (marginal rate 26.5%; CT = 0.265P − 3,750 for a 12-month period with no associated companies).

*Draft prepared for professional review. Figures are GBP, FY2023 (1 April 2023 – 31 March 2024) basis, non-ring fence, 12-month accounting period, no associated companies. Thresholds must be re-scaled for short accounting periods and associated companies before any figure is applied to a real company.*

results.value: marginal relief - main rate 25% reduced by marginal relief, standard fraction 3/200

quotes.whole:
(d) Advanced approaches capital ratio calculations.  An advanced approaches national bank or Federal savings association that has completed the parallel run process and received notification from the OCC pursuant to § 3.121(d) must determine its regulatory capital ratios as described in paragraphs (d)(1) through (3) of this section.
(1) Common equity tier 1 capital ratio.  The national bank's or Federal savings association's common equity tier 1 capital ratio is the lower of:
(i) The ratio of the national bank's or Federal savings association's common equity tier 1 capital to standardized total risk-weighted assets; and
(ii) The ratio of the national bank's or Federal savings association's common equity tier 1 capital to advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets.
(2) Tier 1 capital ratio.  The national bank's or Federal savings association's tier 1 capital ratio is the lower of:
(i) The ratio of the national bank's or Federal savings association's tier 1 capital to standardized total risk-weighted assets; and
(ii) The ratio of the national bank's or Federal savings association's tier 1 capital to advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets.

A custodial bank shall exclude from its total leverage exposure the lesser of:
(A) The amount of funds that the custody bank has on deposit at a qualifying central bank; and

§ 3.10
Minimum capital requirements.
(a)
Minimum capital requirements.
(1) A national bank or Federal savings association must maintain the following minimum capital ratios:
(i) A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent.
(ii) A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent.
(iii) A total capital ratio of 8 percent.
(iv) A leverage ratio of 4 percent.
(v) For advanced approaches national banks or Federal savings associations or, for Category III OCC-regulated institutions, a supplementary leverage ratio of 3 percent.
(vi) For Federal savings associations, a tangible capital ratio of 1.5 percent.
(2) A qualifying community banking organization (as defined in § 3.12), that is subject to the community bank leverage ratio framework (as defined in § 3.12), is considered to have met the minimum capital requirements in this paragraph (a).

Standardized capital ratio calculations.

quotes.whole:
(d)
Advanced approaches capital ratio calculations.
An advanced approaches national bank or Federal savings association that has completed the parallel run process and received notification from the OCC pursuant to § 3.121(d) must determine its regulatory capital ratios as described in paragraphs (d)(1) through (3) of this section.

Common equity tier 1 capital ratio.

(ii) The ratio of the national bank's or Federal savings association's common equity tier 1 capital to advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets.

Tier 1 capital ratio.
The national bank's or Federal savings association's tier 1 capital ratio is the lower of:
(i) The ratio of the national bank's or Federal savings association's tier 1 capital to standardized total risk-weighted assets; and
(ii) The ratio of the national bank's or Federal savings association's tier 1 capital to advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets.
(3)
Total capital ratio.
